question: For $A=\begin{bmatrix}1&2\\3&4\end{bmatrix}$, find $\operatorname{adj}A$ and then calculate $\operatorname{adj}(\operatorname{adj}A)$. Compare the result with $A$.
explanation:
First adjoint
For a matrix of order $2$, interchange the diagonal entries and change the signs of the off-diagonal entries. Thus, $$\operatorname{adj}A=\begin{bmatrix}4&-2\\-3&1\end{bmatrix}$$
Adjoint of the resulting matrix
Applying the same procedure again, $$\operatorname{adj}(\operatorname{adj}A)=\begin{bmatrix}1&2\\3&4\end{bmatrix}$$
Comparison with the original matrix
The resulting matrix is exactly $A$. Therefore, $$\operatorname{adj}(\operatorname{adj}A)=A$$
Conclusion
For the given matrix of order $2$, taking the adjoint twice reproduces the original matrix.
